analysis.evidence: In שלֵימֻונ אַולֵדֿ לַרחַבֿעַמ, Solomon is the subject and the prefixed ל marks Rehoboam as the object. Rehoboam then becomes the subject of the next clause, confirming the father-to-son sequence.
analysis.morphology: Aphel perfect, third person masculine singular, without a pronominal suffix

analysis.evidence: In Matthew 1:7, שלֵימֻונ אַולֵדֿ לַרחַבֿעַמ means “Solomon begot Rehoboam.” The next clause repeats רחַבֿעַמ without the prefix as the subject of “begot Abijah,” confirming both the bearer and the form of the name.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with prefixed לַ־ marking the direct object of אַולֵדֿ, “begot”.
analysis.sense: Rehoboam, son of Solomon and father of Abijah.

analysis.evidence: The preceding clause names Rehoboam as Solomon’s son. The marked occurrence begins רחַבֿעַמ אַולֵדֿ לַאבִֿיָא, “Rehoboam fathered Abijah.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name, without prefix or suffix, serving as the subject of אַולֵדֿ.
analysis.sense: Rehoboam, son of Solomon and father of Abijah.

analysis.evidence: In רחַבֿעַמ אַולֵדֿ לַאבִֿיָא, Rehoboam is the subject and the prefixed ל marks Abijah as the object. Rehoboam fathered Abijah.
analysis.morphology: Aphel perfect, third person masculine singular, without a pronominal suffix

analysis.evidence: In אַבִֿיָא אַולֵדֿ לָאסָא, Abijah is the subject and the prefixed ל marks Asa as the object. The clause identifies Abijah as Asa’s father.
analysis.morphology: Aphʿel perfect, third person masculine singular, without a pronominal suffix.
